author: Alana Loftus
title: Trump surrounded by opulence at Versailles as Americans struggle with the economy - NewsBreak
text:
By Alana Loftus ,
2 hours ago
President Donald Trump enjoyed an evening at one of the most luxurious palaces in the world on Wednesday, as his own country grapples with a cost-of-living crisis.
Trump is currently in France, attending the annual G7 summit. During his time there, Trump has socialized with fellow world leaders, including those with whom the U.S. leader has a contentious relationship. One such leader is French President Emmanuel Macron, who extended a generous invitation to Trump despite having a rocky relationship with him.
Weeks ago, Macron invited Trump to a special, celebratory dinner at the Palace of Versailles, honoring America's 250th birthday and the long-enduring relationship between the U.S. and France.
Trump graciously accepted the invitation, and bragged about the glamorous evening ahead of time, saying, "And then the French president, who happens to be a very nice man, invited me to dinner at Versailles... And Versailles is not a gold leaf. Versailles is the real deal. And I said, 'I'd like to do it.'"
On Wednesday evening, photos emerged from inside the 17th-century castle, commissioned by King Louis XIV. The images showed the level of opulence the palace offers to its esteemed guests, including the U.S. leader who recently claimed that he "loves" inflation.
Trump boasted about his invitation to Chateau de Versailles Trump was pictured walking through the palace, which is decorated in his favorite color, gold. On social media, some users joked that Trump would return from his visit with an ever greater desire to redecorate the White House.
The visit has sparked a conversation about Trump's negligence regarding the economic struggles that everyday Americans are facing. The rising cost of things like gas and groceries has been linked to the Iran war.
Although Washington and Tehran are set to sign a peace agreement this weekend, the war leaves behind massive physical and financial destruction. Trump's war against Iran drove the cost of oil and gas through the roof, as well as the prices of everyday items that were affected by shipping disruptions.
The dinner was hosted by the president and first lady of France A New York Times report released in May found that at least 2/3 of Americans are cutting back on their daily spending habits as the cost of living soars.
When questioned about the pressure the war is putting on American consumers, Trump called the issue "peanuts," and admitted, "I don't even think about that."
